subject: Maths
title: Circumference of a circle
subtitle: Area and Perimeter · KS3 Maths
learning_objective: I can calculate the circumference of a circle using C = πd or C = 2πr.

key_vocab.definition: The circumference is the distance around a circle. The diameter goes across through the centre; the radius is half the diameter.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can calculate the circumference of a circle using C = πd or C = 2πr.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: circumference -- The circumference is the distance around a circle. The diameter goes across through the centre; the radius is half the diameter.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Circumference = π × diameter. If given the radius, double it first (or use C = 2πr).
C = π × d
π is approximately 3.14

Key examples:
  ✓ d = 10 → C = 10π ≈ 31.4 cm  (C = πd)
  ✓ r = 7 → C = 14π ≈ 44.0 cm  (C = 2πr)
  ✓ π ≈ 3.14159...  (irrational number)
  ✗ C = πr (not πd)  (that halves the answer)
  ✗ C = πr²  (that is the area formula)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – given diameter
  Find the circumference of a circle with diameter 8 cm.
  C = πd
  C = π × 8
  C = 25.1 cm (1 d.p.)
  = 25.1 cm
  (Multiply π by the diameter.)

Example 2 – given radius
  Find the circumference of a circle with radius 5 cm.
  C = 2πr
  C = 2 × π × 5
  C = 31.4 cm (1 d.p.)
  = 31.4 cm
  (Double the radius to get the diameter, then multiply by π.)

sections.content:

(b) d = 6 cm

sections.title: Finding radius or diameter
sections.content:
Find the missing measurement (1 d.p.).

(a) C = 62.8 cm; find d
(b) C = 44.0 cm; find r
(c) C = 100 cm; find d
(d) C = 75 cm; find r

sections.title: Word problems
sections.content:
Use π = 3.14. Give answers to 1 d.p.

(a) A circular pond has diameter 4 m. Find circumference.
(b) A wheel has radius 30 cm. Distance in one turn?
(c) A plate has circumference 78.5 cm. Find diameter.
(d) Circular track radius 50 m. Distance for 1 lap?

sections.title: Mixed and semicircles
sections.content:
Find the perimeter of each shape (1 d.p.).

(a) Circle: d = 20 cm
(b) Semicircle: d = 14 cm
(c) Quarter circle: r = 10 cm
(d) Circle: r = 8.5 cm
(e) Semicircle: r = 6 cm

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ C = πd gives the circumference
✗ C = πr² gives the circumference
✓ Diameter = 2 × radius
✗ Semicircle perimeter = half the circumference only
✓ π is approximately 3.14
